deities: Goddess Nanda Devi (incarnation of Parvati/Durga, regarded as Shailputri; rituals follow the tantric tradition as Tara Shakti)
festivals: Nanda Devi Mela (annual September fair around Nandashtami, five days of rituals, folk music, dola procession and stalls)

history.period: 17th century CE (Chand era); popularly described as ~1000 years old - conflicting claims, verify
history.summary: The patron goddess of Kumaon and the family deity of the Chand rulers, enshrined in the heart of Almora's old bazaar (Lala Bazar, Dharanaula). The complex holds three shrines - Parvateshwar, Udyot Chandreshwar and Nanda Devi - showing Chand-era stone carving and Kumaoni woodwork under a stone amalaka (crown). Historical accounts record that in 1688 Udyot Chand erected temples at Almora after victories over Garhwal and Doti, and that the Parbateshwar temple was renamed twice to become the present Nanda Devi temple; Raja Anand Singh later commissioned the idol worshipped today. 'Nanda' means prosperity; the September fair has been held here since Chand times. Some travel sites claim ~1000 years of age, which conflicts with the 17th-century documentary record - flag for verification.

name: Nanda Devi Temple
town_description: Almora is the administrative headquarters of Almora district and the cultural capital of Kumaon, a ridge-top hill station founded as the Chand capital by Raja Kalyan Chand in 1568. It is known for its old bazaars, Kumaoni architecture and cuisine (Bal Mithai), panoramic Himalayan views, and as a base for nearby pilgrim sites like Jageshwar and Kasar Devi.

travel.airport: Pantnagar Airport, the nearest airport (~116-127 km from Almora per travel sources); taxis/buses onward
travel.railway: Kathgodam railway station, the nearest major railhead (~82-90 km from Almora), connected to major cities
travel.road: Almora is ~365 km from Delhi (UTC buses from Anand Vihar ISBT) and ~63 km from Nainital via NH109; the temple is in Lala Bazar, a short walk from the main road

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November (pleasant weather); September brings the Nanda Devi fair and crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 6:00 AM-10:00 PM per srimandir.com (morning aarti 6:00-7:00 AM, evening aarti 7:00-8:00 PM); other sources say sunrise to sunset or 24 hours - verify locally
